newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka sees coconut output rising.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka sees coconut output rising.

text.p: Sri Lanka should increase coconut production to 4.5 billion nuts a year within a decade, the state Coconut Cultivation Board (CCB) said on Thursday.
Officials told Reuters they expected coconut output to improve slightly this year from 1996 levels but said exports would be about the same.
According to the CCB, Sri Lanka produced 2.55 billion nuts in 1996 and exported 608 million.
"If we all go together -- the growers, the government and the researchers -- we should get to 4,500 million in another 10 years time," Sunil Jayasekara, chairman of the CCB, said in an interview.

The chairman of the Coconut Development Authority (CDA), Upali Senaratne, told Reuters Sri Lankan coconut production should rise this year due to better use of fertilisers and an expansion of coconut cultivation into new parts of the island.
"As far as 1997 is concerned, there will be a marginal increase in production," Senaratne said. "Coconut exports should be more or less the same."
